stem: A machine is purchased for Rs 80,000. It is depreciated using the straight-line method at 10% per annum on the original cost. What is the book value of the machine at the end of 4 years?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Annual depreciation = 10% of 80000 = 8000. Over 4 years total depreciation = 32000. Book value = 80000 - 32000 = 48000.
Applies written-down value (reducing balance) at 10% instead of straight-line: 80000 x (0.9)^4 = 80000 x 0.6561 = 52488.
Uses 5 years instead of 4 years: 80000 - 5 x 8000 = 80000 - 40000 = 40000.
Applies 10% on the reduced book value each year (reducing balance) and also uses an incorrect base, arriving at 32000 (= 80000 x 0.4, which is an 8-year straight-line figure).

explanation: Straight-line depreciation charges a fixed amount each year: annual depreciation = cost x rate = 80000 x 10% = 8000. After 4 years: book value = 80000 - (4 x 8000) = 48000.

explanation_sections.punchline: Straight-line depreciation uses the original cost as the base every year, not the reduced balance.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify method: straight-line (SLM). Annual charge = P x r = 80000 x 0.10 = 8000 (constant). Book value after n years = P - n x annual charge = 80000 - 4 x 8000 = 48000.
explanation_sections.lesson: SLM: annual depreciation is always on original cost; WDV: depreciation is on remaining book value (reduces each year).
explanation_sections.timing: 35 seconds. The only trap is confusing SLM with WDV.
